name: Import CSV
notes:
Example interface for importing data provided as CSV.

The interface has three parts:

1. Fetch:
Fetches the data from a storage and iterates over all CSV rows (for the sake of simplicity, the values are not loaded form an external system, but are simply mocked in a TypeScript processor).

2. Process: this part implements the following features

a) verification and mapping
The values of the source data are validated, and external values are mapped to internal ones using the “mappings” collection.

b) import valid records into CRM
If everything is ok, we create a mutation, and the record is written into the CRM. If the mutation was successful, a hash of the record and the created CRM object’s key is stored in the “processedRecords” collection (hang on to understand why).

c) unchanged record detection
Before processing, a record is checked whether it has been changed since its last processing. This reduces processing time of the interface in case the source system is not able to filter those records that have changed since the last execution. Therefore, every imported record is stored in the processedRecords collection, using the object's external key as key and the record's hash as value (note, the hash is computed of all properties).
If the record did change and the hash is different, the "processedRecords" collection also holds the CRM object’s key that has been created before. Hence, we know which one to update.

d) bad record handling
Records for which the verification failed are stored in the "retries" collection as well. The value contains the original record, a reason and a retry counter, initialized with 0. If the record is retired later and if it is still invalid, the counter is incremented.

3. Retry:
The third part of the interface queries the "retries" collection for bad records that have not been retried more than five times. Matching entries are simply processed again.

processors.notes: For the sake of simplicity we use this type script processor to provide some CSV rows. In real life, the data is fetched from a storage, like S3 or FTP.
